text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 35

The panel's composition on its own proves little — in many clinical and hospital hierarchies four senior men is just what the org chart produces, and all-male panels appoint women routinely. Leading with it lets them dismiss you as grievance-driven and shifts the argument to their intentions, which you can't prove.

Your strong facts are concrete: a doctorate and eight years actually running a section versus a master's plus a course, and "broad leadership experience" that is unquantified. Chase the written reasons — escalate to HR in writing, cite any statutory or policy deadline, and ask specifically how each criterion was scored.

Panel composition becomes relevant later, as context, if the reasons turn out to be vague or shifting.
